title: Every card lookup that finds a copy the ledger mirror now has rewrites and fsyncs the whole local-copies file, once per file
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/field_mode.py:737-751 (LedgerView._raw -> local.forget), field_mode.py:684-696 (LocalCopies.forget -> _atomic_write + fsync); via card_verdict (field_service.py:479) and field_copy.py:538 verified_record
what: _raw is a per-file lookup and calls forget() on that file's covered rows; forget() rewrites field-local-copies.jsonl in full with tmp+fsync+replace. The one-time catch-up becomes N rewrites of M rows: O(N x M) bytes and N fsyncs.
cost: First /field/api/state after each ledger sync following a card copy, and every re-run of a card already at a destination. Measured 7.48 s for a 1,000-file card copied to two drives (2,000 rows); at the 60,000-row cap ~6 MB per rewrite, ~6 GB and 1,000 fsyncs for a 1,000-file card (estimated tens of seconds to minutes). The page shows 'Companion not answering' meanwhile.
evidence: probe_forget.py: 7.48 s, all in forget(); code read of _raw/forget/_atomic_write.
fix: Collect covered rows during a verdict / verify loop and flush with one forget() at the end (or lazily). Keep: a covered row is never counted twice (_raw already de-duplicates via seen) and is eventually dropped from disk.

title: A card verdict opens a fresh SQLite connection, re-runs the schema, and linearly scans every local copy, once per file on the card, every 20 s
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/field_mode.py:336 (card_verdict per-file copies_of), field_mode.py:672-682 (LocalCopies.matching full scan); ledger_mirror.py:337-350 + 172-181 (where -> _connect: mkdir, connect, PRAGMA WAL, executescript(SCHEMA)); field_service.py:43 VERDICT_TTL_SECONDS=20, field.js polls state every 4 s (1 s while copying)
what: Per-file lookups each pay connection setup plus schema DDL plus an O(M) Python scan of up to 60,000 local rows; nothing is shared across the files of one verdict.
cost: Per inserted card every 20 s while the field page is open, and after every copy. Measured 0.90 s per verdict at 1,000 files / 4,000 local rows (~4.5% of a core per card); 9.81 s at 2,000 files / 60,000 rows (~50% of a core per card, 10 s state requests), on a field laptop that is also copying.
evidence: probe_verdict.py: mirror.where 1.00-1.34 ms per call, matching 0.154 ms at 4k rows and 3.47 ms at 60k rows, card_verdict 0.90 s and 9.81 s.
fix: One mirror connection per verdict (where_many or a held connection) and SCHEMA once per process; index LocalCopies rows by (name.lower(), size) maintained by add/forget. Keep _present and the mtime slack per row.

title: A dialog that raises on a tray click thread leaves its Tcl interpreter pinned for the life of the process
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/ui_dispatch.py:544-553 (dispatch inline path try/finally reclaim_mine); ui_dispatch.py:146-158 (_Job.run, macOS)
what: When fn raises, reclaim_mine runs while the traceback still holds fn's frame locals (widgets, root), so _try_free sees refs above baseline and keeps the pin. On Windows the building thread is a per-click _spawn thread or the per-open work-window thread and exits next, so the interpreter can never be freed.
cost: ~1.8 MB per failed dialog build, permanent; triggers are TclErrors from RDP reconnects or display changes mid-build. Rare: a few MB a month on a machine RDP'd into daily, plus a WARNING with holder chains each time.
evidence: probe_pin.py with a fake root/tkapp: return path leaves 0 pinned after the thread exits, raise path leaves 1 pinned on a dead thread with the module's own 'still referenced (5 refs, baseline 4)' warning.
fix: Catch BaseException, traceback.clear_frames(exc.__traceback__), then reclaim_mine, then re-raise, in dispatch() and _Job.run. Pin-at-birth and free-on-building-thread rules are untouched.

title: The menu fingerprint carries lane C's live byte and file counts, so the menu is rebuilt every tick while lane C uploads
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/tray.py:3942-3945 (_menu_fingerprint includes raw s.detail); sync/syncthing_lane.py:921-929 (detail embeds counts and sizes); tray.py:5252-5255; tray_native.py:1883-1889 -> _build_nsmenu on macOS
what: The fingerprint is deliberately coarse everywhere else but includes each lane's raw detail, which for lane C embeds moving counts, so every changed count is a full _build_menu and on macOS a full NSMenu rebuild with new ObjC targets on the Tk-Aqua main thread.
cost: Up to 43,200 rebuilds a day during lane C uploads instead of on state changes (probe: 300 distinct fingerprints in 300 ticks). Windows: nil (~6 us build, free assignment). macOS: estimated 1-3 ms of main-thread work per rebuild.
evidence: probe_snapshot.py fingerprint churn; code read of the fingerprint and the darwin __setattr__ hook.
fix: Fingerprint a digit-normalised detail (replace each run of digits with '#'); the live numbers stay on the tooltip, as the fingerprint's own docstring intends.

title: The 2 s tray tick re-reads and re-parses site.json three times, and the pulse thread wakes 2.7 times a second with nothing to pulse
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/tray.py:2962, 2971-2975 (cached_site via _dashboard_url and three feature_enabled calls), tray.py:3002/2531 (second app.lane_statuses() per tick), tray.py:5276-5309 (pulse loop sleeps 0.375 s forever)
what: site._brand_site already memoises the manifest by mtime for exactly this caller, but cached_site/feature_enabled (what the tray calls) re-read and re-parse the file every time. The pulse thread polls a tuple every 375 ms even when nothing pulses.
cost: Per machine per day: 216,000 small file opens (130,000 site.json parses) through on-access scanning, plus ~230,000 pulse-thread wakeups. Measured snapshot total 0.33 ms per tick (~15 CPU-s a day), so the saving is wakeups and disk I/O beside Resolve.
evidence: probe_snapshot.py: 5 read_text per snapshot (site.json x3, eula_accepted.json, ytdl-attestation.json), 0.317 ms per snapshot.
ledger: related to comp-app-4; new for the site.json half
fix: Route feature_enabled() with no site argument through _brand_site() (still fail-closed); pass the snapshot's statuses into _current_project_line; let the pulse loop wait on an Event set when pulsing starts.
